title: Shadow-to-Owner 7-day Handoff and Skill Solidification Checklist
body:
Purpose:
A lightweight, practical 7-day checklist for converting a new hire or internal transfer from 'shadow' to full owner of a small infra/platform responsibility. Focus is on compact learning objectives, observable acceptance criteria, and risk signals for people-ops and the mentor. This doc is intentionally pragmatic: short tasks, paired verification, and a clear rollback plan.

Context and scope:
- Intended for engineers joining a pod who need quick ownership of a single on-call runbook, a deploy pipeline step, or a monitoring dashboard.
- Not a full 90-day plan; this is the first-week solidification after initial access + orientation.
- Works for internal transfers and external hires.

Quick definitions (for reviewers):
- Shadow: observed work, asked questions, completed guided walkthroughs.
- Owner: can execute the task without hand-holding, detect anomalies, and escalate appropriately.
- Mentor: the primary trainer for the 7-day handoff.

Success criteria (what "owner" means here):
- Completes the core runbook/playbook end-to-end without prompts in a simulated or low-risk real environment.
- Explains three failure modes and remediation for the owned area.
- Can point to two relevant observability metrics and interpret them.
- Creates or updates one small automation/script to remove a manual step (or opens a linked ticket).

Day-by-day checklist (compact):
Day 0 (pre-week):
- Mentor ensures all accesses are provisioned: repo, cluster, monitoring, pager, docs. Verify with a smoke checklist link.
- New hire receives short primer doc + 10-min orientation calendar block.
- Quick low-risk lab environment prepared (staging branch or sandbox project).

Day 1: Survey + runbook walkthrough
- 30m: Mentor walkthrough of the owned surface area, scope, and why it matters.
- 60m: Guided read-through of the canonical runbook (identify unclear steps).
- Task: New hire writes a one-paragraph summary of ownership responsibilities and posts to team channel.
- Acceptance: Mentor verifies summary and highlights one correction if needed.

Day 2: Read + replicate
- Task: Execute the main safe-to-run checklist in staging/sandbox (deploy, backfill cache, reindex, etc.). Mentor observes.
- Task: Reproduce a documented test incident (simulated) and walk through remediation.
- Acceptance: New hire executes end-to-end and records short session notes or a screencast.

Day 3: Metrics + alerting understanding
- Task: Pair with SRE/observability owner for 45m to map metrics and alerts to customer impact.
- Task: Annotate two alerts with runbook links and suggested threshold tweaks (instrumentation note).
- Acceptance: Mentor verifies annotations and marks safe-to-change for one non-critical threshold.

Day 4: Small automation + code ownership
- Task: Identify a trivial manual step to automate (script/CI tweak) and prototype it.
- Task: Open a PR with test coverage or a clear follow-up ticket if prototype too big.
- Acceptance: PR opened OR ticket created and prioritized in backlog.

Day 5: Incident simulation + async handoff
- Task: Run a brief incident drill (can be tabletop or simulated low-risk incident). New hire leads the page, triage, and postmortem notes.
- Task: Draft a concise ownership README in the repo or Confluence (2–3 sections: what I own, how to escalate, quick commands).
- Acceptance: README posted and mentor + oncall buddy sign-off.

Day 6: Customer/consumer sync + permissions review
- Task: Meet (15–30m) with the primary consumer team or product PM to confirm expectations and SLAs.
- Task: Re-run access checklist; remove any temporary mentor tokens.
- Acceptance: Consumer gives a green-light or notes a prioritized follow-up.

Day 7: Final verification and official handover
- Task: New hire performs the core task (deploy/runbook) end-to-end unobserved while mentor watches passively.
- Task: Owner posts final note: "I am comfortable owning X with Y caveats" and files owner sign-off in the onboarding tracker.
- Acceptance: Mentor & team lead sign off in tracker. If any gap remains, plan a targeted 3-day remediation with clear owners.

Observable acceptance checklist (for sign-off):
- Core task executed without prompts: yes/no
- Three failure modes explained: yes/no
- Observability metrics identified: yes/no
- PR/ticket opened for automation: yes/no
- README posted and acknowledged: yes/no

Risk signals (red flags) and recommended mitigations:
- Red flag: Repeated inability to reproduce a safe test incident. Mitigation: schedule extra pairing sessions and assign a 48h buddy.
- Red flag: Critical access dependencies still missing after Day 3. Mitigation: escalate to people-ops and block hiring checklist until resolved.
- Red flag: Cannot explain why alerts correlate to customer impact. Mitigation: require redo of Day 3 pairing and add a short quiz.

Mentor responsibilities and coaching tips:
- Keep sessions short: 30–60m focused blocks with hands-on steps.
- Use scaffolding: start with exact commands then gradually remove prompts.
- Document decisions in the runbook as they happen.
- Prefer "show me" over long explanations; ask the new hire to teach-back.

Interview rubric tie-in (how hiring signals map to 7-day outcomes):
- Puzzle/problem-solving signal (during interview): maps to ability to reproduce incidents on Day 2. If interview showed weak debugging skills, plan more guided labs.
- Ownership signal (behavioral): maps to Day 5 incident leadership and README ownership. Low signal -> mentor escalate to 3-day remediation.
- Systems intuition (back-of-envelope infra design): maps to Day 3 metrics mapping. Weakness -> assign short learning module on observability fundamentals.

Quick templates (copy/paste into team channel):
- New hire summary template: "I will own [area], main contacts are [mentor, pm], core commands: [cmds], escalation: [pager/team]."
- Mentor sign-off template: "I confirm [name] completed 7-day handoff for [area] — issues: [if any]."

Fallback and remediation plan:
- If sign-off fails: schedule a focused 3-day remediation with the mentor and a peer buddy. Define 3 measurable milestones and a follow-up sign-off.
- If remediation fails: notify hiring manager + people-ops to determine a longer-term plan (training extension, role adjustment).

Notes to people-ops (operational):
- Maintain a small checklist artifact in HR tracker for rapid verification of access items — this doc references confluence:ONBOARD-1123.
- Consider pairing new hires with a non-mentor buddy for the first week to reduce mentor load.
- Track common friction points across handoffs and feed them back into interview rubric calibration.

Unresolved questions / things to iterate on:
- What qualifies as a "trivial" automation? Define a max-LOE (e.g., <3 engineer-hours) for the 7-day scope.
- Should we require a short quiz for metrics understanding? Pilot on two pods first.
- How to encode this sign-off into our HR system for visibility to people managers?

Appendix: quick access checklist (copy to pre-week email)
- Repo access: yes/no
- Staging project: yes/no
- Pager and oncall rotation: yes/no
- Monitoring dashboard link: [paste link]
- Runbook link: [paste link]
- Mentor booked: [name, calendar invite]

A note on tone: keep templates short and asynchronous-friendly. The aim is to move someone from passive observer to reliable owner fast while minimizing mentor context-switch overhead.

Change log:
- 2026-01-11: first draft by Ayesha Khan
- 2026-02-03: edits from Marcus Li and Sofia Martinez - added remediation plan and interview rubric tie-ins

End of document.
